body:
uv 0.13.9 and main lock crate versions that have published RustSec advisories, where the fixed releases are already semver-compatible with uv's dependency requirements, so a `cargo update` should be enough:

| Crate | Locked | Fixed in | Advisories |
|---|---|---|---|
| zstd-safe | 7.2.4, 8.0.0 | 7.4.0, 8.2.0 | RUSTSEC-2026-0396 … -0406 (e.g. RUSTSEC-2026-0400 `DCtx::decompress*`, RUSTSEC-2026-0403 `DCtx::decompress_stream`) |
| zstd | 0.13.3, 0.14.0 | 0.13.4, 0.14.3 | RUSTSEC-2026-0391 |
| icu_normalizer | 2.1.1 | 2.3.0 | GHSA-3jjw-63vg-v3hh |
| ctutils | 0.4.2 | 0.4.4 | RUSTSEC-2026-0385 |

`zstd` 0.13.3 requires `zstd-safe ^7.1`, `zstd` 0.14.0 and `compression-codecs` 0.4.45 require `zstd-safe ^8`, and `idna_adapter` requires `icu_normalizer ^2.2`, so all of these are lockfile-only. Some of these advisories sit behind features uv does not enable (`experimental`, `seekable`, `zstdmt`), but the decompression ones (RUSTSEC-2026-0400 and -0403) are on the path `async-compression`'s `ZstdDecoder` uses when uv extracts `.tar.zst` archives.

Scanners flag every uv binary for these today. Would you be open to a lockfile refresh in the next release? Related: #23279 (rsa 0.10 via reqsign).
title: Refresh Cargo.lock to pick up fixed zstd, zstd-safe, icu_normalizer and ctutils (RustSec advisories)
